rose.name: Rose
rose.habitat: Cultivated worldwide, especially in temperate regions. Thrives in well-drained soil and sunny locations.
rose.description: Used for skin care and in cosmetics. The petals have anti-inflammatory properties and are often used in face masks and lotions.
rose.precautions: Generally safe, but people with plant allergies should be cautious.

tulsi.name: Tulsi
tulsi.habitat: Native to the Indian subcontinent, grows in tropical and subtropical climates. Prefers sunny locations and well-drained soil.
tulsi.description: Used in Ayurveda for its medicinal properties. It is believed to enhance immunity and relieve stress.
tulsi.precautions: Avoid during pregnancy without consulting a healthcare provider. May lower blood sugar.

aloevera.name: Aloevera
aloevera.habitat: Native to the Arabian Peninsula, but cultivated worldwide. Thrives in arid and semi-arid regions with well-drained soil.
aloevera.description: Known for its soothing and healing properties. Often used to treat burns, cuts, and other skin issues.
medicinal_uses: Topical treatment for burns and cuts
aloevera.precautions: Do not consume the whole leaf; only use the inner gel. Oral consumption can have a laxative effect.

lavender.name: Lavender
lavender.habitat: Native to the Mediterranean region. Grows well in dry, sandy, or gravelly soils and prefers full sun.
lavender.description: Used in aromatherapy for relaxation and sleep improvement. The scent is known for its calming effects.
lavender.precautions: Undiluted essential oil can irritate the skin. Do not ingest essential oil.

mint.name: Mint
mint.habitat: Widely distributed in temperate regions. Prefers moist, fertile soil and partial shade but can tolerate full sun.
mint.description: Commonly used to aid digestion and relieve headaches. Mint leaves can be used in teas and culinary dishes.
mint.precautions: Can cause heartburn in some people. Avoid large amounts during pregnancy.

chamomile.name: Chamomile
chamomile.habitat: Native to Europe and Western Asia. Grows in well-drained soil with full sun exposure.
chamomile.description: Used to promote relaxation and help with sleep. Chamomile tea is a popular remedy for insomnia and anxiety.
chamomile.precautions: People with ragweed allergies may have a reaction. Avoid if on blood thinners.

dandelion.name: Dandelion
dandelion.habitat: Native to Eurasia and North America. Thrives in a variety of soil types and can grow in both sunny and shaded areas.
dandelion.description: Used as a diuretic and to aid digestion. The leaves, roots, and flowers are used in various herbal remedies.
dandelion.precautions: May cause an allergic reaction in some people. Consult a doctor if you have gallbladder issues.

ginger.name: Ginger
ginger.habitat: Native to Southeast Asia. Grows well in tropical and subtropical climates with rich, well-drained soil and partial shade.
ginger.description: Known for its anti-nausea and anti-inflammatory properties. It is commonly used in cooking and as a remedy for nausea.
ginger.precautions: May interact with blood-thinning medications. Can cause heartburn in some individuals.

turmeric.name: Turmeric
turmeric.habitat: Native to tropical South Asia. Prefers warm, humid climates with well-drained, fertile soil.
turmeric.description: Contains curcumin, which has anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects. Often used in cooking and for its health benefits.
turmeric.precautions: Can act as a blood thinner. Avoid if you have gallbladder problems or are pregnant.

parsley.name: Parsley
parsley.habitat: Native to the Mediterranean region. Grows well in fertile, well-drained soil with partial shade.
parsley.description: Rich in vitamins and used for its diuretic properties. Parsley is also a common garnish and has various health benefits.
parsley.precautions: Pregnant women should consume in moderation, as high doses may affect uterine contractions.

thyme.name: Thyme
thyme.habitat: Native to the Mediterranean region. Prefers dry, well-drained soil and full sun exposure.
thyme.description: Has antimicrobial properties and is used in cooking and medicine. Thyme is also used in traditional remedies for respiratory conditions.
thyme.precautions: Thyme oil can be irritating to the skin. Avoid large amounts if pregnant.

rosemary.name: Rosemary
rosemary.habitat: Native to the Mediterranean region. Thrives in well-drained soil and full sun.
rosemary.description: Used to improve memory and concentration, and for its antioxidant properties. Rosemary is commonly used in culinary dishes.
rosemary.precautions: High doses can be dangerous. Avoid if pregnant or if you have seizures.

sage.name: Sage
sage.habitat: Native to the Mediterranean region. Grows well in dry, sandy soil and full sun.
sage.description: Known for its digestive benefits and antimicrobial properties. Sage is often used in cooking and herbal medicine.
preparation_methods: Fresh or dried leaves for cooking
sage.precautions: Excessive use of common sage can be toxic due to a compound called thujone. Avoid large doses if pregnant.

oregano.name: Oregano
oregano.habitat: Native to Europe, the Mediterranean region, and Western Asia. Prefers dry, well-drained soil and full sun.
oregano.description: Contains antioxidants and is used for its anti-inflammatory effects. Oregano is commonly used in Italian cuisine and traditional medicine.
oregano.precautions: Oregano oil can be very potent and should be diluted. Not recommended for pregnant women in medicinal amounts.

coriander.name: Coriander
coriander.habitat: Native to regions spanning from Southern Europe and Northern Africa to Western Asia. Thrives in well-drained soil with full sun.
coriander.description: Used for its antioxidant and digestive benefits. Coriander seeds are used as a spice, and the leaves are used in salads and dishes.
coriander.precautions: Generally safe. Can cause a minor allergic reaction in some individuals.

fennel.name: Fennel
fennel.habitat: Native to the Mediterranean region. Grows well in well-drained soil and full sun.
fennel.description: Known for its digestive benefits and ability to reduce bloating. Fennel seeds are used in cooking and traditional remedies.
fennel.precautions: May interact with certain medications. High doses are not recommended for pregnant or breastfeeding women.

jasmine.name: Jasmine
jasmine.habitat: Native to tropical and subtropical regions. Prefers well-drained soil and full sun to partial shade.
jasmine.description: Used in aromatherapy for its calming effects and to reduce stress. Jasmine flowers are also used in perfumes and teas.
jasmine.precautions: Generally safe. Pregnant women should consult a doctor before using jasmine oil.

hibiscus.name: Hibiscus
hibiscus.habitat: Native to tropical and subtropical regions. Thrives in warm climates with well-drained soil.
hibiscus.description: Rich in antioxidants and used to lower blood pressure. Hibiscus tea is a popular beverage known for its tart flavor.
hibiscus.precautions: Can significantly lower blood pressure. May interact with blood pressure medications.

echinacea.name: Echinacea
echinacea.habitat: Native to North America. Prefers well-drained soil and full sun.
echinacea.description: Boosts the immune system and is used to prevent colds. Echinacea is often used in herbal supplements and teas.
echinacea.precautions: People with autoimmune disorders should consult a doctor. Short-term use is recommended.

banana.name: Banana
banana.habitat: Native to Southeast Asia, now grown worldwide in tropical climates. Requires warm temperatures and moist, fertile soil.
banana.description: Rich in potassium and dietary fiber. Used as an energy source and for digestive health.
banana.precautions: People with a latex allergy may have a cross-reaction to bananas.

bilimbi.name: Bilimbi
bilimbi.habitat: Native to Southeast Asia. Prefers warm, humid climates and well-drained soil.
bilimbi.description: Fruit is sour and used in traditional medicine to lower cholesterol and control hypertension.
bilimbi.precautions: High in oxalic acid, so consume in moderation, especially if you have kidney issues.

cantaloupe.name: Cantaloupe
cantaloupe.habitat: Cultivated in warm regions worldwide. Prefers sandy loam soil and full sunlight.
cantaloupe.description: Rich in vitamin C and antioxidants. Helps with hydration and immune support.
cantaloupe.precautions: Generally safe. Wash the rind thoroughly before cutting to avoid bacterial contamination.

cassava.name: Cassava
cassava.habitat: Native to South America, widely cultivated in tropical regions. Grows in poor, sandy soils.
cassava.description: Staple root crop rich in carbohydrates. Used to make flour, tapioca, and traditional foods.
cassava.precautions: Must be properly peeled and cooked to remove cyanide compounds. Never eat raw.

coconut.name: Coconut
coconut.habitat: Tropical coastal regions worldwide. Requires sandy soil and high humidity.
coconut.description: Fruit provides water, milk, oil, and fiber. Used in food, cosmetics, and medicine.
coconut.precautions: High in saturated fat, so consume oil in moderation.

corn.name: Corn
corn.habitat: Native to the Americas, cultivated globally. Grows well in warm climates and fertile soil.
corn.description: Staple cereal crop rich in carbohydrates. Used as food, livestock feed, and biofuel.
corn.precautions: Generally safe. Can be difficult to digest for some people.

cucumber.name: Cucumber
cucumber.habitat: Native to South Asia, cultivated worldwide. Prefers warm climates with moist soil.
cucumber.description: High in water content, promotes hydration and skin health. Commonly eaten fresh or pickled.
cucumber.precautions: Generally safe. People with a pollen-food allergy syndrome may have a reaction.

curcuma.name: Curcuma
curcuma.habitat: Native to tropical South Asia. Thrives in warm, humid regions with fertile soil.
curcuma.description: Includes turmeric species, used for anti-inflammatory and antioxidant purposes.
curcuma.precautions: Can act as a blood thinner. Avoid if you have gallbladder problems or are pregnant.

eggplant.name: Eggplant
eggplant.habitat: Native to Asia, cultivated globally. Prefers warm climates with well-drained soil.
eggplant.description: Rich in fiber, antioxidants, and vitamins. Used in various cuisines worldwide.
eggplant.precautions: People with nightshade sensitivity may have a reaction. Avoid eating raw.

galangal.name: Galangal
galangal.habitat: Native to Southeast Asia. Thrives in tropical climates with moist, fertile soil.
galangal.description: Used in Asian cuisine and traditional medicine. Believed to improve digestion and reduce inflammation.
galangal.precautions: Generally safe in culinary amounts. Medicinal doses should be discussed with a doctor.

guava.name: Guava
guava.habitat: Native to Central America, now cultivated in tropical regions worldwide. Grows in various soils.
guava.description: Rich in vitamin C and antioxidants. Used to boost immunity and digestion.
guava.precautions: Eating too many guavas can cause bloating.

kale.name: Kale
kale.habitat: Native to the Mediterranean. Grows well in cool climates with moist, fertile soil.
kale.description: Leafy green vegetable high in vitamins A, C, and K. Known as a superfood.
kale.precautions: Can interfere with blood-thinning medications due to high Vitamin K content. People with thyroid issues should consume in moderation.

longbeans.name: Longbeans
longbeans.habitat: Native to Africa, widely cultivated in Asia. Prefers warm climates with well-drained soil.
longbeans.description: Rich in fiber and protein. Commonly used in Asian stir-fries and salads.
longbeans.precautions: Generally safe. Best to cook before consumption.

mango.name: Mango
mango.habitat: Native to South Asia. Grows best in tropical and subtropical climates.
mango.description: Tropical fruit rich in vitamins A and C. Known for its sweet flavor and health benefits.
mango.precautions: People with a poison ivy/oak/sumac allergy may have a cross-reaction to the mango peel.

melon.name: Melon
melon.habitat: Cultivated worldwide in warm climates. Requires well-drained soil and full sun.
melon.description: Includes many varieties like honeydew and muskmelon. Hydrating and rich in vitamins.
melon.precautions: Wash the rind thoroughly before cutting to avoid bacterial contamination.

orange.name: Orange
orange.habitat: Native to Asia, cultivated worldwide in subtropical climates.
orange.description: Citrus fruit high in vitamin C. Boosts immunity and is used in juices, oils, and cosmetics.
orange.precautions: High acidity may cause irritation for people with acid reflux.

paddy.name: Paddy
paddy.habitat: Native to Asia, cultivated in flooded fields in tropical and subtropical regions.
paddy.description: Rice plant, staple food for over half the world’s population.
paddy.precautions: Excessive consumption of polished white rice can lead to blood sugar spikes.

papaya.name: Papaya
papaya.habitat: Native to the tropics of the Americas. Thrives in warm, humid regions.
papaya.description: Rich in vitamin C and digestive enzyme papain. Helps with digestion and skin care.
papaya.precautions: Unripe papaya contains a latex that can trigger contractions. Avoid during pregnancy.

pepper_chili.name: Chili Pepper
pepper_chili.habitat: Native to the Americas, now cultivated globally. Prefers warm climates.
pepper_chili.description: Rich in capsaicin, known for its spicy flavor and metabolic benefits.
pepper_chili.precautions: Can cause digestive upset in some people. Avoid touching eyes after handling.

pineapple.name: Pineapple
pineapple.habitat: Native to South America, cultivated in tropical regions.
pineapple.description: Tropical fruit rich in vitamin C and bromelain enzyme. Aids digestion and boosts immunity.
pineapple.precautions: Can cause an allergic reaction. The bromelain can cause a tingling sensation in the mouth.

pomelo.name: Pomelo
pomelo.habitat: Native to Southeast Asia. Grows in tropical and subtropical climates.
pomelo.description: Largest citrus fruit, rich in vitamin C and antioxidants.
pomelo.precautions: Can interact with certain medications, similar to grapefruit.

shallot.name: Shallot
shallot.habitat: Native to Central or Southwest Asia, cultivated worldwide.
shallot.description: Aromatic bulb with antioxidant and antibacterial properties. Used in cooking and medicine.
shallot.precautions: Generally safe. People with onion allergies should be cautious.

soybeans.name: Soybeans
soybeans.habitat: Native to East Asia, cultivated worldwide. Prefers warm climates.
soybeans.description: Rich in protein and used for soy products like tofu, soy milk, and soy sauce.
soybeans.precautions: Can cause digestive issues in some people. Can affect thyroid function in large amounts.

spinach.name: Spinach
spinach.habitat: Native to Persia, cultivated globally. Prefers cool climates with moist, fertile soil.
spinach.description: Leafy green vegetable rich in iron, vitamins, and antioxidants.
spinach.precautions: High in oxalates, which can interfere with mineral absorption and contribute to kidney stones. People with kidney issues should consume in moderation.

sweet_potatoes.name: Sweet Potatoes
sweet_potatoes.habitat: Native to Central and South America. Grows in tropical and subtropical climates.
sweet_potatoes.description: Rich in fiber, vitamins, and antioxidants. Used as a staple food in many cultures.
sweet_potatoes.precautions: Generally safe. Can cause bloating in some people.

tobacco.name: Tobacco
tobacco.habitat: Native to the Americas, cultivated worldwide in warm climates.
tobacco.description: Cultivated for its leaves, primarily used for smoking and nicotine extraction.
tobacco.precautions: Highly addictive and a major cause of cancer and heart disease. Not for medicinal use without medical supervision.

waterapple.name: Waterapple
waterapple.habitat: Native to Southeast Asia. Grows in tropical, humid climates.
waterapple.description: Tropical fruit with hydrating properties. Sweet and crunchy, used fresh or in salads.

watermelon.name: Watermelon
watermelon.habitat: Native to Africa, cultivated worldwide in warm climates.
watermelon.description: Hydrating fruit rich in lycopene and vitamins. Promotes hydration and heart health.
watermelon.precautions: Can cause digestive upset in some people due to high water and fructose content.
